idiom_name: std::variant<Cases...> + std::visit with an overload set
implementation_notes: Modern C++ closes a variant set with std::variant<Circle, Rect, Triangle> and dispatches with std::visit over an overload set (template<class... Ts> struct overloads : Ts... { using Ts::operator()...; }), which is the closest C++ gets to a compiler-checked exhaustive match: the call does not compile when the visitor cannot be invoked with every alternative. C++ cannot seal a class hierarchy - final closes a single class, not a set - so the sum type, not the inheritance tree, is the closed set, and operations are free functions over it. Use this form for value-semantic data with operations added often; keep virtual dispatch or a visitor when cases must participate in an open hierarchy or carry identity and polymorphism.
pitfalls: A generic lambda [](const auto&) or a base-class overload in the set absorbs an unhandled alternative and silently disables the compile-time coverage check.
All arms must produce the same return type (or an explicit R): libstdc++ rejects a visitor whose arms disagree with a static_assert on the visit result type.
std::variant has a valueless_by_exception state and std::visit then throws std::bad_variant_access; alternatives must also be copyable/movable for many operations.

variants.name: Hand-rolled tag + union with a checked switch (pre-C++17 / freestanding)
variants.idiom_name: enum class tag + union payload + switch under -Wswitch-enum
variants.implementation_notes: Where <variant> is unavailable - older standards, freestanding/embedded toolchains that exclude exceptions and RTTI - the closed set is hand-rolled instead: a struct with an enum class tag and a union of per-variant payloads, constructors that set the tag and placement-new the active member, and one switch per operation compiled with -Wswitch-enum plus a std::abort()/assert(false) default. The compiler still does not know the set, so the guarantee degrades to a warning plus the unreachable-default convention; keep this form only where std::variant cannot be used, and even there prefer it to a hand-written Visitor.
pitfalls: Union members with non-trivial constructors or destructors must be managed by hand (placement new plus explicit destructor calls); this hand-rolled variant is where lifetime bugs live.
The trailing abort() is mandatory for the function to return on all paths, but replacing it with a silent fallback disables the very warning the construction relies on.
Compilers warn per switch, not per hierarchy: -Wswitch-enum is silenced by a default arm and must be enabled and curated explicitly.
